Designs¶

Designs for a particular setting, course, population or product: what a design uses the general patterns for. A pattern is general across contexts; a design is not.

D¶

  • D-PBL weekly activity pattern: small-group PBL with branching case decisions and facilitated debate - This pattern organizes a PBL module so each week's case is a branching virtual patient worked by a small group of 6-8 learners.

  • DAA activities as reverse discovery: a discovery-based pedagogy that starts with the expert artefact - Disassemble/Analyze/Assemble (DAA) activities are described as an inherently discovery-based pedagogy that starts with the artefact, an instance of a typically well-engineered solution.

  • Dative alternation training task presented as a simple structural change - The learning target and task of the experiment: the English dative alternation, an abstract generalization that learners tend to overgeneralize.

  • DCog model of debriefing as a coordination device for conversational remembering and distributed metacognition - The article reconceptualises the three-phase simulation debriefing through distributed cognition, arguing that the debriefing conversation itself is the major coordination device.
  • Debate learning model for yellow book study combining independent guidance, classroom activities, and dormitory activity - The article proposes a debate model for yellow book learning structured in three linked components: guidance independent, activities in the classroom, and activity in dormitory, culminating in outputs of new knowledge...
  • Debriefing with good judgment: a reflective-practice debriefing method using performance gaps to explore learner frames - Debriefing with good judgment is a well-established debriefing method in which the debriefer uses observations of performance gaps to explore learner frames and thought processes.
  • Debugging assignments built around the three error types of quantum programs - Debugging assignments deepen proficiency with course programming tools and introduce the debugging step of the quantum software development cycle.
  • Decision making about the future learning outcome framework with twelve components - The article develops a 'decision making about the future' learning outcome framework informed by decision-making science, AI methodologies, and educational and psychological perspectives.

  • Decision-PBL (D-PBL): branching virtual patient cases with structured debate at management decision points - D-PBL is a variant of problem-based learning that replaces linear paper cases with Web-based branching virtual patients.
  • Decoding/Fluency tutoring program: 20-week adaptive one-on-one intervention with six scripted lesson components - A one-on-one decoding and fluency treatment delivered over 20 weeks using 10 books ordered by reading difficulty, with placement and lesson repetition/skipping adaptive to student performance.
